title: Causal Chain Decomposition of Benchmark Contamination to Deployment Harm

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: maps contamination through score inflation to deployment harm, identifying which causal link is weakest. Directly guides where to invest mitigation effort.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Deliberately contaminating benchmarks via fine-tuning requires advanced ML expertise, access to model training pipelines, and significant compute beyond Colab Pro.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple stages (contaminate training data, measure score inflation, test OOD safety probes) make this a multi-component project well beyond 30 hours for beginners.

novelty.reasoning: Benchmark contamination is extensively studied with surveys (arxiv 2406.04244, 2502.14425), controlled contamination experiments showing 5-15% accuracy distortion, and multiple mitigation strategies (AntiLeakBench, watermarking). The causal chain from contamination to inflated scores is well-documented. However, the specific decomposition tracing contamination through to deployment harm via safety-specific benchmarks, identifying which causal link is weakest, has not been the focus of published work. The contamination side is largely addressed; the deployment harm side is novel.
